forecast-period.text: A ridge of high pressure continues to build across the state. The high will move across the Bight and into the Tasman Sea early next week as another trough begins to develop over WA.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Isolated showers about the agricultural area, most likely about coastal parts and the Lower South East. Slight chance of a thunderstorm about the southeast. Dry elsewhere. Maximum temperatures near average to below average. Fresh and gusty south to southwesterly winds.

Isolated showers about the southern agricultural area and west coast, becoming more likely during the afternoon and evening. Dry elsewhere. Maximum temperatures below average. South to southeasterly winds, fresh at times during the day.
Light morning showers about the southern agricultural area. Maximum temperatures below average. Dry elsewhere. South to southeasterly winds, fresh about the northeast.

text.p: Dry. Maximum temperatures below average in the northeast, grading to above average in the south. East to northeasterly winds.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Tuesday: 2 to 5 mm across the agricultural areas, West Coast and east of the Flinders Ranges, increasing to 5 to 15 mm in the Riverland and southeast. Isolated falls of 30 to 40 mm are possible with thunderstorms during Friday.
